blocks.content: Constitutional bodies derive their powers, status, and authority directly from the Constitution of India.

rows: Directly from the Constitution of India
Election Commission, UPSC, Finance Commission, CAG
Enacted by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature
NHRC, SEBI, NGT, Central Vigilance Commission
Requires ordinary legislative amendment or repeal
NITI Aayog, Law Commission of India
Can be created or dissolved by executive decision alone

items: Match the Constitutional Body with its correct Article (e.g., CAG: Art 148, Finance Commission: Art 280, UPSC: Art 315, Election Commission: Art 324).
Distinguish between Constitutional bodies (enumerated in text), Statutory bodies (created by Parliamentary Act), and Executive bodies (created by Cabinet resolution).
Pay attention to the appointing authority and security of tenure guaranteed to constitutional heads by the President of India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Constitutional bodies derive their authority directly from specific articles of the Constitution of India.
Article 324 establishes the Election Commission of India to superintend, direct, and control elections.
Article 280 mandates the President of India to constitute a Finance Commission every fifth year.
Article 315 provides for the establishment of the Union Public Service Commission and State Public Service Commissions.
Article 148 creates the independent office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India as the custodian of public funds.
